To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

, when a monkey performs an identification task using either familiar or unfamiliar faces, the activities of the population in the ventral portion in the anterior inferior temporal (AITv) cortex are differentially organized to represent the faces in the two categories.

the neuronal representation of personally familiar faces in the AItv neuronal population is characterized by a high degree of identity specificity and low degree of view specificity, while the neuronal representation of unfamiliar faces is characterized by a low degree of identity specificity but a high degree of view specificity.

, in the AIT of monkeys, the neuronal representations of familiar faces and unfamiliar faces are different, and that the difference is reflected in the similarity/dissimilarities among the faces in the neuronal population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the neuronal mechanisms underlying visual perception in the primate brain.

the neural representations of personally familiar or unfamiliar facial identities and views in the AIT, which is the most anterior and ventral part of the ventral temporal pathway for visual object recognition.
the neural mechanisms underlying the representation of personally familiar and personally unfamiliar faces in primates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
personally familiar faces are represented by a pattern of activities of a population in the AIT, while unfamiliar faces are represented by another pattern of activities of the same population.
the neuronal representations of the personally familiar and unfamiliar facial stimuli are not the same in the AIT neuronal population.

the AITv neurons in the macaque monkeys represent personally familiar faces by encoding the facial identity irrespective of their views, but represent personally unfamiliar faces by encoding their views irrespective of their facial identities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the neural representations of personally familiar faces in the AItv are characterized by the independence of the facial identities and the dependence of the views, whereas those for personally unfamiliar faces are characterized by the dependence of the identities and the independence of the views.

the AITv neurons represent faces in the form of the face identity and the face view in the case of personally familiar faces, whereas they represent faces in the forms of the face identity, the face view, and the face familiarity in the case of unfamiliar faces.
the AITv neurons represent the personally familiar faces by their facial identities and views, while they do not represent the personally unfamiliar faces as well as they do the familiar ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neuronal representations of personally unfamiliar faces are different from those of personally familiar faces in the Aitv.

the AITv neurons are capable of representing different views of the same face as well as different identities of the faces presented in the same view, and the representation is dependent on the personal familiarity of faces.

the neuronal representations of faces are different between the two categories of faces, which may be due to the different degrees of familiarity or the differences in the processing mechanisms for the two categories of stimuli.
